newsitem.title: CHINA: China interbank market rates (CHIBOR) mixed.
newsitem.headline: China interbank market rates (CHIBOR) mixed.

text.p: Following is the China Interbank Offered Rate (CHIBOR) for Tuesday issued by the official Xinhua news agency on behalf of the People's Bank of China, the central bank.
The figures represent weighted averages and not closing
prices and are annual percentage rates.
Turnover rose sharply to 6.7 billion yuan from 1.9 billion yuan with the one-day contract the most active.

Traders said the turnover surged today due to a sharp rise in volume in the three-day contract on a rumour that a meeting was going on in Beijing to discuss the enforcement of a ban on state banks trading on the state debt secondary market.

At a meeting last week, the central bank told state banks to phase out their trading on the state debt repurchase market to drive bank money out of the stock market. The banks were told not to build new positions but offset existing positions.
Central bank officials declined to comment on the rumour.

Traders said if the ban was effectively enforced, securities houses would rely more on interbank market trading, in particular the short-term contracts, for funds which led to the one-day contract becoming the most active today.

"The rumour said that the central bank will enforce the ban on state banks trading on the repo market immediately," said one trader. "If the rumour is confirmed, trading in short-term contracts will surge in the short term."
But if the rumours on the meeting were not confirmed, then turnover on the interbank market will shrink again shortly, traders said.
